title: FakeDOS for macOS
excerpt: The most realistic DOS since DOS. A screen saver that turns your idle Mac into a 1990s PC.
content_html:
FakeDOS 2.0 · Screen saver for macOS

The most realistic DOS since DOS.

Leave your Mac alone for a few minutes and it becomes a 1990s PC: an AWARD BIOS counts through 32 MB of RAM, a VGA prompt starts blinking, and then a ghost begins to type. It boots. It crashes. It dials. It lies convincingly.

v2.0 · macOS 13+ · Universal Binary · free

C:\> TYPE README.TXT

What is this?

Welcome, traveller. You have just discovered FakeDOS, a macOS screen saver that simulates a pixel-perfect DOS machine. And more.

Leave your Mac alone for a few minutes and something beautiful is going to happen: the screen fills with the warm 80×25 glow of a VGA text mode, an AWARD BIOS POST clicks through memory, and a friendly blinking C:\> prompt appears.

Perfect for

  • A conference room that does not need Slack popping up
  • Pretending to be a 12-year-old running Landmark Test
  • Tricking a co-worker into thinking you have lost it
  • Actually getting people to leave you alone

Features

The Ghost Writer

Leave the prompt idle and a ghost starts typing commands by itself. It alternates between operating systems in an endless loop of simulated productivity.

  • Many DOS commands, boot linux, some Linux commands, boot dos, repeat
  • Realistic typing speed with human-like typos
  • Press any key to take over and the ghost vanishes

Warp 5

Speeds up everything, not just the ghost. 1 is slow, 9 skips all delays.

Landmark speed test

Type FDOS or LANDMARK at the prompt to see how fast your imaginary Pentium thinks it is.

IBM PC/XT4.77 MHz

IBM AT8 MHz

486DX33 MHz

Your Pentium166 MHz

Pure nostalgia, zero benchmarking.

Pentagon mode

Type PENTAGON at the prompt. We cannot tell you what happens.

ACCESS DENIED. CLASSIFIED.

This is not a real DOS.

  • OKYour files are safe.
  • OKYour disk is safe.
  • OKYour Mac is safe.
  • OKYour network is safe.

Absolutely nothing useful happens here.

FakeDOS is a pure simulation. Every single command you type produces carefully crafted fake output. No files are read, written, moved or deleted. No network connections are made. No processes are started. No disks are formatted.

When you type FORMAT C:, FakeDOS shows a terrifyingly realistic format sequence, complete with percentage counter and head/cylinder display, but your actual drive is perfectly untouched. When you type DEL *.*, nothing gets deleted. Ever.

It simulates. It pretends. It lies convincingly.
But it never, ever touches your real system.

Not a terminal. Not an emulator. Not connected to the Pentagon. Probably.

C:\> HELP

Commands

DIR
List files in current directory

CD
Change directory

TYPE
Display file contents

COPY
Copy files

MOVE
Move files

DEL
Delete files (fake!)

REN
Rename files

MKDIR
Create directory

TREE
Show directory tree

CLS
Clear screen

CHKDSK
Check disk

FORMAT
Fake format (scary!)

MEM
Show memory map

VER
MS-DOS version

DATE / TIME
Current date and time

BOOT
Switch to DOS / Linux / C64

LM
Landmark speed test

PENTAGON
CLASSIFIED

???
CLASSIFIED

EXIT
Quit FakeDOS

Arrow keys scroll through the command history.

Download FakeDOS

FakeDOS.dmg v2.0 · macOS 13+ · Universal Binary · 4.2 MB

Downloads since launch 0000000

Psst... the boss thinks C:\ is empty. Type DIR anyway. Some files in the root directory were never meant for office hours.

Installation

  1. Drag FakeDOS.app into /Applications.
  2. Double-click to launch. It installs itself as a menu-bar icon.
  3. Click the menu-bar icon to configure or start manually.
  4. After the configured idle time (default: 5 min), FakeDOS takes over fullscreen.
  5. Type EXIT to return to your real desktop.

Cmd + , opens six pages of pure control: idle time, warp speed, the ghost writer, sound and more. The PC speaker can be silenced. Your co-workers cannot.

Version 2.0 for macOS

FakeDOS started in 1991 as a Turbo Pascal prank on a FidoNet BBS and lived its first life as a screen saver for Microsoft Windows.

Three decades later, it was ported to Swift/macOS so it can terrorize modern office workers who have never heard of AUTOEXEC.BAT.

Klaus Rössler & Roger Kirchhoff
Copyright (c) 1991 - 2026
